key_insight: Fine-tuned transformer models, especially FLAN-T5-Large, can accurately detect social isolation and social support cues in unstructured clinical notes.
clinical_relevance: This could help health systems flag patients at risk of social isolation earlier using existing EHR text, supporting more context-aware population health workflows.
method: Annotated clinical note spans with social context cues from 326,847 adults aged 50+ years.
Fine-tuned FLAN-T5-Large, BERT, RoBERTa, and Gemma-2-2B using structured prompts.
Compared models with Accuracy, Precision, Recall, and Macro-F1 to reduce false positives and overgeneralization.
evidence_signal: FLAN-T5-Large performed best with Macro-F1 0.92 ± 0.04, outperforming Gemma-2-2B (0.89 ± 0.10), RoBERTa (0.80 ± 0.21), and BERT (0.77 ± 0.17).
watch_item: Performance was evaluated on annotated notes, so real-world deployment still needs external validation, monitoring for domain shift, and careful handling of ambiguous or negated language.
paper_title: Fine-Tuned Large Language Models for Detecting Social Isolation from Unstructured Clinical Notes
